03 / Known concerns

What Mercedes-Benz
owners ask about.

Common topics for these cars. Not every car develops them — a diagnosis comes first, then a clear recommendation.

Airmatic air suspension

S-Class, E-Class, GL/GLS and more

A car sitting low after it’s been parked, or a suspension warning on the dash.

Balance shaft & timing

M272 V6 and M273 V8 engines, around 2005–2008

Check-engine codes for camshaft and crankshaft correlation.

7G-Tronic transmission

722.9 conductor plate and valve body

Harsh shifts, limp mode or speed-sensor faults.

Oil leaks & oil coolers

Oil cooler and filter-housing seals on many V6 and V8 engines

An oil smell under the hood or drips beneath the engine.

SBC brakes

W211 E-Class and R230 SL

Sensotronic brake warnings need careful diagnosis.

Electrical & battery

Batteries, sensors and control modules

Houston heat shortens battery life, and low voltage can trigger a cascade of warnings.

05 / Questions

Good to
know.

Something else on your mind? Ask in your request, or call the shop.

Do I have to use the dealer to keep my Mercedes-Benz warranty?+

Generally, no. Under the federal Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act, a manufacturer can’t void your warranty or deny coverage just because maintenance was done by an independent shop.

Follow the factory maintenance schedule and keep your records. Repairs covered by the warranty itself are still handled by the dealer.

Are you affiliated with Porsche, BMW or Mercedes-Benz?+

No. Houston Auto Pros is an independent shop that focuses on these makes. It isn’t affiliated with, or endorsed by, any manufacturer.

What happens after I send a request?+

A request isn’t a confirmed booking. The shop reviews it and contacts you to confirm a time and talk through what your car needs.
